claim: LLM self-improvement (model verifies its own outputs, filters/reweights data by that verification, distills the filtered data) is governed by a formalized 'generation-verification gap' that scales monotonically with the model's pretraining FLOPs.
stance_target: the hypothesis that self-refinement's helpfulness is model-scale dependent, and that a small model's self-refinement failure is scale-predictable rather than novel
scope_conditions: various model families and tasks, ICLR 2025
quoted_support: we discover a scaling phenomenon of self-improvement -- a variant of the generation-verification gap scales monotonically with the model pre-training flops.

claim: The paper provides a mathematical/modular framework for exactly when iterative self-improvement is possible at all, plus an iterative self-improvement procedure and methods to improve its performance, meaning the boundary conditions under which self-refinement helps vs. hurts are already an object of formal study as of ICLR 2025.
stance_target: whether 'small model self-refinement fails' is a settled/confirmatory finding vs. a novel contribution
scope_conditions: ICLR 2025, controlled modular study of self-improvement
quoted_support: we initiate a comprehensive, modular and controlled study on LLM self-improvement... We also examine when self-improvement is possible, an iterative self-improvement procedure, and ways to improve its performance.
